title: Fields are excellent
statement: Every field $k$, regarded as a commutative ring, is excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring].

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary field $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring], $k$ is Noetherian and regular, its only prime ideal is $(0)$, and $k_{(0)}\cong k$. Under this identification the maximal ideal is zero and the residue field is $k$. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], its completion is also $k$: for $n\ge1$ all quotients $k/(0)^n$ are $k$ and all transition maps are identities, so a compatible sequence is constant. The possible $n=0$ coordinate is uniquely determined. This identifies the canonical completion homomorphism with $\operatorname{id}_k$.

source.place: Tag 07PX (proposition-ubiquity-G-ring), field case; elementary zero-adic completion calculation from the definition.

proof.text: The identity map of $k$ is flat in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]: the mutually inverse maps $N\otimes_k k\to N$, $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, and $N\to N\otimes_k k$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, identify tensoring any injective map with that same map. Its unique fibre is $k\otimes_k k\cong k$, by the analogous multiplication and unit maps. For every finite purely inseparable extension $k'/k$, the further tensor product $k'\otimes_k k\cong k'$ is a regular Noetherian ring by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring] applied to the field $k'$. Thus the fibre is geometrically regular by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], without assuming that $k$ is perfect. The completion map in step 1 is therefore regular, and that definition, together with the Noetherianity in step 1 and the fact that $(0)$ is the only prime, proves that $k$ is a G-ring.

source.place: Tag 07PX (proposition-ubiquity-G-ring), proof of (1), with the identity-map, fibre and geometric-regularity verifications expanded.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-j2-residue-field-criterion] to $R=k$, which is Noetherian by step 1. The only prime is $(0)$ and its residue field is $k$. Given any finite purely inseparable extension $L/k$, take the $k$-subalgebra $B=L\subseteq L$. It is finite as a $k$-module by the finite-dimensionality assumption in [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Its fractions exhaust $L$, since every $x\in L$ is $x/1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring] every localization of the field $L$ is regular local. Its spectrum is nonempty (the prime $(0)$ exists), so $U=\operatorname{Spec}L$ is the required nonempty open regular subset. Every hypothesis of the criterion is now satisfied; its conclusion is exactly the openness of the regular locus of every finite type $k$-algebra, the J-2 condition.

source.place: Tag 07PJ (proposition-ubiquity-J-2), proof of (1), checking condition (4) of Tag 07PC (lemma-J-2).

proof.text: Let $A$ be any finite type $k$-algebra. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], choose a surjective $k$-algebra map $\pi:P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to A$, with kernel $I$. Pullback of ideals gives an order-preserving bijection between prime ideals of $A$ and primes of $P$ containing $I$: its inverse sends $Q\supseteq I$ to $\pi(Q)$, which is an ideal by surjectivity; $A/\pi(Q)\cong P/Q$ via $\pi$, so primality is equivalent, and $\pi^{-1}(\pi(Q))=Q$ because $I\subseteq Q$. For primes $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ of $A$ write $\mathfrak p',\mathfrak q'$ for their pullbacks. Every finite chain between them pulls back to a strict chain below $\mathfrak q'$, hence has length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')\le n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-chain-height-difference] and its definition of height. Saturation is preserved: any prime strictly between two pulled-back primes contains $\mathfrak p'\supseteq I$, so descends to an intermediate prime of $A$. That theorem now says that every saturated chain from $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak q$ has the same length $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p')$. Thus every finite type $k$-algebra is catenary, including the finite-chain bound required in [def-exc-excellent-ring]; if $A=0$ there are no prime pairs and the assertion is vacuous. This proves universal catenarity of $k$.

source.place: Tag 00OR (lemma-dimension-height-polynomial-ring); the elementary passage along a surjective polynomial presentation is written out. This supplies the universal-catenarity input of Tag 07QW without a new Cohen-Macaulay lemma.

proof.text: The arbitrary field $k$ is Noetherian by step 1, a G-ring by step 2, J-2 by step 3 and universally catenary by step 4. These are exactly the conditions defining excellence in [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Therefore every field is excellent.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07QW (proposition-ubiquity-excellent), clause (1): its G-ring and J-2 route is expanded using 07PX, 07PJ and 07PC.
